brief: Goldman's Nelson Armbrust tracks two threads. First, L/S Fundamental hedge funds continue lagging Systematic funds: fundamental L/S fell -1.02% last week versus MSCI World +0.35%, while systematic L/S rose +1.28%. Year-to-date, fundamental funds are +12%, mostly Asian investor driven, with US funds at +8%, versus systematic funds' +20%. Breadth confirms the divergence: under 30% of S&P stocks trade above their 50-day moving average. Sentiment has followed: GS's Sentiment Indicator fell to -0.9, its lowest in over a year, and AAII bearish sentiment jumped 14 points week-over-week to 53.3%, highest since May 2025, as bullish sentiment fell to 28.8%. Second, Meta's Muse consumer AI agent, released September 8, hit #1 among free US Apple apps within a week, with Apptopia estimating 1.6mm US downloads in eight days versus ChatGPT's ~822k in its own first eight days. The buzz is bidding up the AI complex, driving CPU plays INTC and ARM up 5% on the agent-momentum trade. The note argues the CPU/cloud compute trade deserves attention alongside GPUs.
